settings.title: Settings
settings.acctOutHint: Without signing in, Persist Notes opens in read-only mode for your meetings. Sign in to record, import, summarize, and ask.
settings.keepAudio: Keep the audio (.wav) in an audio/ subfolder
settings.systemAudio: Also capture the computer audio (participants on Teams, Meet, Zoom)
settings.myVoiceHint: Lets the app recognize you in the computer audio. It stays on this computer only and never goes to Claude.
settings.diarize: Separate the participants' voices (Person 1, Person 2…), on your computer
settings.calendar: Calendar (to suggest the title and guest names)
settings.calPlaceholder: Paste your calendar's iCal link here (one per line) or the path to an .ics file
settings.calHelp: Google Calendar: Settings → your calendar → Secret address in iCal format. Outlook: Settings → Calendar → Shared calendars → Publish a calendar → ICS link. The link stays on this computer only.
settings.voiceOffHint: Automatically recognizes, in upcoming meetings, the people you've already named. Uses voice prints stored on this computer only. Off by default.
settings.liveHint: Transcription happens during the meeting, in the background and at low priority, so it doesn't get in the way of Teams, Meet, or Zoom. Fewer cores keep the call lighter; more cores get the note ready faster. Once the recording ends, the app uses all of them.
settings.claudeHint: Uses your Claude subscription: install Claude Code and run claude once in the terminal to sign in. Persist Notes removes the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY variable when calling Claude, so you aren't charged for API usage.
settings.mcpHint: Connects Persist Notes to Claude as a source: Claude can then search meetings, decisions, Commitments, and project syntheses. Read-only.
settings.diarNoEngine: The voice separation component isn't available in this installation.
settings.diarReady: All set: voices in the system audio are separated when transcribing.
settings.diarNeeded: Needed to separate voices ({size}, one time only).
settings.permNative: The computer's sound uses the System Audio Recording Only permission (Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording). If you open Persist Notes from the terminal (npm start), the terminal app (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code…) is the one that needs the permission.
settings.permOld: On this macOS, the computer's sound requires the Screen & System Audio Recording permission. The system asks on the first recording.
settings.needClaude: install and sign in to Claude Code (for summaries)
settings.mcpCodeDone: ✓ Done. Open a new Claude Code session and ask about your meetings.
settings.mcpDesktopDone: ✓ Configured in {file}. Quit and reopen Claude Desktop to turn it on.
settings.calEmpty: Paste an iCal link or choose an .ics file first.
settings.calOk: ✓ {count} events read · {next} in the next 7 days.
settings.meetingDetect: Ask whether to record when a meeting starts
settings.meetingDetectHint: Persist Notes notices when one of these apps starts using the microphone (the same signal that turns on the orange indicator in macOS). Nothing is recorded unless you choose Record.
settings.muteShortcutHint: The shortcuts work even with Persist Notes in the background, only while recording. Click the field and press the key combination.
settings.micDeviceHint: If the chosen microphone isn’t connected, Persist Notes records with the system default and lets you know.
settings.whisperBuiltin: Built into the app (whisper.cpp {version}). Nothing to install.
settings.whisperSystem: Using the system whisper-cli ({path}) because the built-in one did not work on this computer.

voice.nobody: Nobody registered yet: name the participants of a meeting (click "Person 1"…) and Persist Notes learns their voice.
voice.disableConfirm: Delete all voice prints and turn off recognition? The names already written in your meetings stay.
voice.consentIntro: When you turn this on, Persist Notes creates a voice print (a set of numbers that represents the timbre) for each person you name in the transcripts, and uses these prints to recognize those people in upcoming meetings.
voice.consentBio: Biometric data: under privacy laws such as Brazil’s LGPD and the GDPR, a voice print is sensitive personal data.
voice.consentLocal: On this computer only: the prints stay in the app's data folder, outside the notes folder. They're never sent to Claude or to any server, and they don't go along if you sync or share the notes folder.
voice.consentControl: You're in control: in Settings you can see who's registered, delete one person, or delete everything. Turning it off deletes all prints (your own voice profile has its own Delete button).
voice.consentWarn: Tell the participants: you're responsible for informing the people being recorded and, when required, getting their consent.
voice.consentAgree: I have read and agree to the use of voice prints described above.

selfVoice.title: Record my voice
selfVoice.intro: The app will record about 15 seconds of you reading a short text and store a profile of your voice (a set of numbers that represents the timbre). With it, the app recognizes you when your voice shows up in the computer audio and doesn't create an extra "Person".
selfVoice.itemBio: Biometric data (under privacy laws such as Brazil’s LGPD and the GDPR): it stays on this computer only, in the app's data folder. It never goes to Claude, to the .md files, or to any server.
selfVoice.itemDelete: You can delete the profile at any time in Settings → Recording.
selfVoice.readHint: Read in your normal voice, as in a meeting:
selfVoice.readText: Good morning, everyone. Let's start with today's agenda: first the status of this week's deliverables, then the project risks, and finally everyone's next steps. If anyone has an urgent topic, feel free to bring it up now, before we move on.
selfVoice.savedText: Voice profile saved {when}, with the label "{name}".
selfVoice.noneText: No profile recorded: the app uses your speech on the microphone in each recording.
selfVoice.stopFirst: Stop the recording before recording your voice.
selfVoice.saved: Your voice profile was saved on this computer.
